sentences.text:
Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HC-3725 asserting that on 07.06.2020 at about 2.30 p.m. to 3.00 p.m. when riding a motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HC-3725 on Bidarakere- Jagalur road, near Madakari farm,
Gopagondanahalli village, Jagalur Taluk, Davanagere District, rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HC-4974, rode the same negligently from the opposite direction, dashed the same to motorcycle bearing No. KA-17-HC- 3725, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.

2. Petitioner took treatment at Government Hospital, Jagalur and S.S Hitech Hospital,
Daavanagere.
As on the date of accident petitioner being aged about 40 years, used to earn Rs.18,000/p.m. by working as Supervisor at T.T. Agro Fertilizer and doing agriculture.

3. Regarding accident Jagalur police registered crime No.95/2020 against the rider of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HC-4974.
4.
In spite of service notice, respondent No.1-owner of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HC-4974 remained absent.

5. In response to the notice respondent No.2- insurance company appeared through his Advocate and filed written statement denying the reason and mode of accident nature and consequences of injuries suffered by petitioner.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 22.07.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues :
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that on 07.06.2020 at about 2.30 p.m. to 3.00 p.m. on Bidarekere- Jagaluru road, near Madakari Farm,
Gopagondanahali village, Jagalur Taluk, Davangere District, in view of the negligent use of the Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-17-HC- 4974 accident taken place resulting in the injuries to the petitioner?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled to compensation ? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order ?
7. On 26.07.2023, 03.09.2024, petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 21 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.21.

Through court commissioner, petitioner recorded evidence of Dr. Manjunath as PW.2 and produced 3 documents at Ex.P.22 to P.24.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of petitioner and respondent No.2 and perused the records.

9. On the basis of the record, my findings on the above issues are as under:

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence petitioner stated that on 07.06.2020 at about 2.30 p.m. to 3.00 p.m. when riding a motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HC-3725 on Bidarakere- Jagalur road, near Madakari farm, Gopagondanahalli village, Jagalur Taluk, Davanagere District, rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HC-4974, rode the same negligently from the opposite direction, dashed the same to motorcycle bearing No. KA-17-HC- 3725, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
11. In the written statement respondent No.2- insurance company denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.

12. In the cross-examination petitioner stated that during accident Yekanthappa was not present in the place of accident, after the accident Manju resident of Bidarikere village shifted him to Government Hospital, Jagaluru.
Petitioner submitted ignorance about the name of the person who informed about the accident to Manju, Bidarikere.
Petitioner stated that when Kotresh and Peersab provided first aid, he was unconscious.
PW.1 submitted ignorance about the contents wrote by doctors of Government hospital, Jagalur, in the medical records.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that head on collision taken place between 2 motorcycles.

Petitioner denied the suggestion that he rode the motorcycle in high speed, lost balance, dashed the same to another motorcycle, thereby caused accident, there was no negligence or error on the part of the rider of the another motorcycle for the alleged accident.
13.
In the evidence affidavit PW.2 - Dr. Manjunath J. stated nothing about the reason and mode of the accident.

14. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR and complaint pertaining to crime No.95/2020 registered by Jagalur police on 15.06.2020 against Darshan S/o Shivanna- rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HC-4974 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,337 of IPC regarding accident taken place on 07.06.2020 at 14.30 hours between motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HC 3725 and KA-17-HC-4974 resulting in the injuries to the petitioner on the basis of the complaint presented by Ekanthappa D. S/o Late Gurudsiddappa.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of the notice dated 16.06.2020 issued by the police to Panchayathdhars.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of the sketch of place of accident.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of the certificate under Sec.65(B) of Evidence Act issued by PC No.442, Jagaluru police station.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of the motorcycle seizure mahazar dated 16.06.2020.
Ex.P.6 is the motor vehicle accident report dated 19.06.2020.
Ex.P.7 is the copy of the wound certificate issued by SSIMS hospital, Davanagere in which reason for the injuries is noted as on 07.06.2020 at 2.30 p.m. RTA near Besthuvalli, Jagalur.

Ex.P.8 are statements of Gurumurthi Gurumurthy D.A vs Shivanna on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143208745/
3 D.A./petitioner S/o Ekanthappa dated 17.07.2020, Hussain Peer Sab S/o Imam Ali dated 16.06.2020, Kotresha S/o Hemanna dated 16.06.2020, Hemanth Kumar K.S. S/o Sangappa dated 17.07.2020 recorded by I.O. Ex.P.9 is the copy of the charge sheet filed by Jagalur police in crime No.95/2020 against Darshan S/o Shivanna rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HC- 4974 and Shivanna S/o Erappa -respondent No.1/owner of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HC-4974 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,337,338 of IPC and Sec.3, 181, 180, 5, 181 of MV Act.

sentences.text: In the discharge summary history of the injuries are noted as RTA on 07.06.2020 at around 2.10 p.m. near Jagalur.
15. In this case respondent No.1- owner of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HC-4974 remained absent.
16. In this case there are no reasons to disbelieve the contents of the police records and evidence of PW.1 regarding the reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 07.06.2020 at about 2.30 p.m. to 3.00 p.m. when petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HC-3725 on Bidarakere- Jagalur road, near Madakari farm, Gopagondanahalli village,
Jagalur Taluk, Davanagere District, Darshan S/o Shivanna -rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HC-4974, rode the same negligently from the opposite direction, dashed the same to motorcycle bearing No. KA-17-HC- 3725, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
Hence , I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:

In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident he has suffered grievous injuries i.e., displaced fracture right hand, right 2 nd and 3rd metatarsal bone, chip fracture of medial end of right 1 st proximal phalanx, comminuted fracture proximal end of right tibia extending to metaphysis, took first aid treatment at Government Hospital, Jagaluru and then took treatment at S.S. Hitech Hospital, Davanagere as inpatient from 07.06.2020 to 22.06.2020 and again from 30.07.2020 to 06.08.2020, underwent surgery by spending Rs.3,03,000/-.

Petitioner stated that as on the date of accident used to earn Rs.30,000/-p.m. by working as Supervisor at T.T. Agro Fertilizers, Jagalur and doing agriculture.
18.
In the written statement, respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

19. In the cross-examination petitioner denied the suggestion about non-spending of Rs.3,00,000/-
for treatment, nourishment etc.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that as on the date of accident he neither working as a Supervisor at T.T. Agro Fertilizers, Jagaluru nor earned Rs.30,000/- per month .
Petitioner has denied the suggestion about fabricating of medical bills worth of Rs.1,54,769/- for the purpose of this case.
20. In the evidence PW.2-Dr. Manjunath stated about the treatment provided to petitioner at SSIMS & RC hospital, Davanagere.
PW.2 stated that on 15.05.2024 when clinically examined the petitioner noticed that petitioner suffered permanent physical disability at 20% to right lower limb.
In the evidence PW.2 produced case sheet, disability certificate and C.T. Scan film at Ex.P.21 to P.23.

In the cross-examination PW.2 admitted that fractures of the petitioner are united and denied the Gurumurthy D.A vs Shivanna on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143208745/
4 suggestion about removal of implants.

entities.text: Gurumurthy D.A vs Shivanna on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: PW.2 explained that implants are not removed from the radius.
PW.2 admitted that petitioner never suffered loss of muscle power.

21. Wound certificate, discharge summaries, medical bills, prescriptions, case sheets, OPD records,
X-rays and other medical records shows that in the accident petitioner suffered traumatic tibial plateau fracture (Schatzker type VI) with IC 2nd and 3rd metatarsal fracture, swelling deformity over right leg , abnormal mobility of both chest and right foot, took treatment at SSIMS Hospital,
Davanagere as inpatient from 07.06.2020 to 22.06.2020 and from 30.07.2020 to 06.08.2020 by spending approximately Rs.1,54,769/-.
22.
In the Driving Licence marked at Ex.P.11 the date of birth of the petitioner is noted as 20.05.1973.
In the copy of the Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P.12 the date birth of the petitioner is noted as 23.05.1975.

In the copy of income tax returns for the assessment year 2020-2021 declared income of the petitioner is noted as Rs.8,61,380/- and Rs.1,00,540/- is noted as tax paid under certificate marked at Ex.P.14 dated 01.10.2021 Proprietor of T.T. Agro Fertilizers certified that since last 2 years petitioner is working as Agriculture Supervisor monthly salary of Rs.22,500/-, TA and DA Rs.7,500/- and since 07.06.2020 due to physical disability suffered in view of accident removed from the job.
23.
In the file there are no documents regarding quantum of the income of the petitioner immediately prior to the date of accident.
In this case there are no documents regarding decrease in the income of the petitioner or loss of income of the petitioner subsequent to the treatment taken for the injuries suffered in the accident.

Certificate marked at Ex.P.14 alleged to have been issued by Proprietor T.T. Agro fertilizers is not supported by any documentary evidence (attendance register,
payment register etc.)

Hence, I have inferred that the oral evidence of PW.2 Dr.Manjunath and certificate marked at Ex.P.14 are insufficient to award compensation under the head loss of future income(Permanent Physical Disability).
24.

Considering the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner, length, place and nature of treatment taken by the petitioner, I award compensation Rs.1,00,000/-towards pain and suffering,
Rs.1,54,769/- towards medical expenses, Rs.30,000/- towards attendant conveyance and nourishment charges, Rs.1,45,000/- (Rs.14,500/- x 10), towards loss of income during treatment period and Rs.80,000/- towards loss of amenities and future happiness.
25. Hence, I came to the conclusion that petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.5,09,769/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. as compensation.
Hence, I answer Issue No.2 accordingly.

Issue No.3:
26.
In the written statement, respondent No.2 insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HC-4974 as on the date of accident.

In para No.9 of written statement the respondent No.2-insurance company asserted that the police have filed charge sheet alleging that Darshan S/o Shivanna/ respondent No.1 was not holding a valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident, thereby committed offence punishable under Gurumurthy D.A vs Shivanna on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143208745/
5 Sec.3, 181, 5 of MV Act, therefore the respondent No.1 violated the terms of the police.
Therefore respondent No.1 is not entitle to indemnify.

As referred above the charge sheet is filed against Darshan S/o Shivanna-respondent No.1 and respondent No.1 for having committed offence punishable under Sec.279, 337, and 338 of IPC and Sec.3, 5, 181 of MV Act.
Hence, it is clear that respondent No.1 - Shivanna violated the driver clause of the policy.

27. In the lengthy argument the learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that respondent No.2- insurance company has to pay compensation amount then recover the same from the respondent No.1 by relying on the following judgments:
1. (2018) 3 Supreme Court Cases 208- DD.19.01.2018 - in between Pappu and others V/s Vinod Kumar Lamba and another.

entities.text: Pappu and others V/s Vinod Kumar Lamba and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2. MFA No.7089/2016 c/w MFA No.6824/2016 - D.D. 19.09.20204- The Legal Manager, Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd.

V/s Smt. Nagamma & others C/w Smt. Nagamma & others V/s P.
Venkatesh & others.

28. As per the recent opinion of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka whenever owners (insured) of the vehicle violated the driver clause of the policy such owners have to pay compensation to the petitioners or to dependents of the victim.

According to the recent opinion of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka whenever owners of the vehicles (Insured) have violated permit/FC clause of the policy, the insurance company (insurer) are bound to deposit compensation amount, then entitle to recover the same from the insured.
As referred above, in this case respondent No.1- Shivanna - owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HC-4974 violated the driver clause of the policy.

Hence,
in this case respondent No.1 - Shivanna S/o Erappa has to deposit the compensation amount.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondent No.1 being the owner of the Motorcycle bearing No. KA-17-HC-4974 is liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondent No.1 to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.3 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.

The respondent No.1 shall pay Rs.5,09,769/- (Rupees Five lakhs nine thousand seven hundred sixty nine only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.1, being the owner of the Motorcycle bearing No. KA-17-HC-4974 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 4 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
